title: LLM modes cannot reject false positives; llm_max_requests is hard-coded
description: 1) --use-llm (hybrid) asks the LLM only for fields with no match or max confidence < 50, so false matches at 85-99 are never reviewed (armsis: 89 -> 90 false). 2) llm_max_requests=100 is a CrafterCmd default with no CLI/config setting; a file with 105 fields makes --llm-only fail after 100 requests ('LLM request budget exceeded' -> 'LLM classification failed'). 3) A verifier prototype (rules propose candidates, one LLM request per table with masked values, keep plausible ids) gave 0 false and 38-41 of 44 correct on armsis for 0.001-0.007 USD; consider an opt-in --llm-verify mode after the deterministic gates.
close_reason: llm_max_requests is configurable (.metacrafter, --llm-max-requests), the budget error names the setting, a warning precedes it; docs state that hybrid mode does not review rule matches. The LLM verifier mode is tracked separately.

title: metacrafter-rules: person_name rules and extension field names
description: AU, IN and SG rule files map full-name field rules to key person_name, whose registry record is a draft Chinese type (country CN), and the only universal-looking name matches come from those country files; with --country-codes am no person_name rule loads. firstname/lastname keys are the Indian registry records. A universal full-name datatype and rule are missing. Also no field rule maps 'extension'/'file_ext' to file_extension (registry draft, generic regexp), so GeoNode links.extension stays unlabelled.

title: Decide --country-codes semantics for universal rules (country_code: xx)
description: --country-codes am loads only rule files whose country_code includes am; files with country_code: xx (universal rules: email, uuid, city, description...) are dropped (processor.py import_rules). On armsis GeoNode metadata --country-codes am cut correct matches from 44 to 23. --langs drops lang: common the same way, and docs say 'Only load US/Canada rules', so this may be intended, but a scan with a country set most likely wants universal plus that country's rules. Options: treat xx as always included for scans, or add a flag.
close_reason: Decided: --langs/--country-codes select language- and country-specific rule files; lang: common and country_code: xx (or none) always load. Implemented in update-rule-filters-and-name-evidence; armsis --country-codes am: 23 -> 45 correct matches.

title: Opt-in LLM verifier mode (--llm-verify) for rule candidates
description: Hybrid mode only labels fields that rules left unlabelled; it cannot remove false matches. Prototype: rules propose candidates, one LLM request per table with masked value shapes, sibling column paths and candidate descriptions; the model keeps plausible ids. On armsis GeoNode metadata: 0 false and 38-41 of 44 correct (gpt-4o-mini, claude-haiku-5.5, gpt-5-mini, claude-sonnet-5.5), 0.001-0.025 USD per table. After the deterministic gates it catches semantic name collisions (CKAN 'state' is a record status, not a state; package_id is not package_name). It drops correct field-name matches on empty columns, so run it on value matches only. Needs an OpenSpec proposal.

title: Fix overly broad regexps and wrong countries in metacrafter-registry
description: Found while fixing false positives (update-detector-false-positive-gates). Registry regexps that accept ordinary tokens: flightnumber has the alternative |\d{1,4} (any 1-4 digit number), udkindex \d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3})*, quarter [1234], unclass [3789], miccode ^[A-Z0-9]{4}$, eunuts/vatin accept any 3-letter acronym. Metacrafter now requires field-name evidence for them, but the regexps should be tightened or marked as needing context in the registry. Country data looks wrong for generic types: person_name -> CN, firstname/lastname -> IN. 84 of 346 stable regexps reach background broadness 0.3 (metacrafter/engine/background.py).
notes: metacrafter-registry branch claude/fp-followups (commit b35d9ec): flightnumber without |\d{1,4}, eunuts and vatin with country prefixes, wkt stable; validate/build/pytest pass. PR not opened yet. Countries: person_name (CN) and firstname/lastname (IN) are intended country records; the mismatch is in metacrafter-rules (separate issue). Then bump the bundled registry snapshot in metacrafter.

title: Build registry-derived detectors from pattern records (iso639_1, iso639_2)
description: ISO 639 codes are registry patterns (semantic_type: language), not datatypes, and add_registry_detectors only uses kind: datatype records; they are also draft. A detector from a pattern record would report its semantic_type with the pattern id (as qddate matches do) and use the semantic_type name as field-name evidence, so a column 'language' with 'eng' reports language/iso639_2. Found on armsis GeoNode metadata (language: eng, owner.language: en).
